title: AI-Based eXtended Reality Training for Automation
summary: BSD design is developing XTENDIT, AI-based extended-reality training in automation skills for industrial workers, and reports no learning or onboarding result.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: BSD design, of Milan, Italy, is developing XTENDIT with the University of Bologna. XTENDIT uses AI and extended reality to train industrial workers in automation skills. BSD design plans to assess participants' skills before, during and after the training. The submission reports no learning, onboarding or production result, so these outcomes remain intended.
purpose: Help industrial workers acquire skills for automated production.

ratings.reason: Industrial workers are intended to gain automation skills and problem-solving capability.
Manufacturers and trainers are intended to improve onboarding and reduce rework; no observed result is supplied.

data.answer:
BSD design proposes AI-supported extended-reality training to improve workers' automation skills. Learning, production, and onboarding outcomes are not reported.

The benefits section names intended measures such as output, downtime, errors, and onboarding time but supplies no assessed changes in those measures. Better automation skills cannot be inferred solely from the use of extended reality or adaptive interfaces.

The account does not separately assess AI’s contribution to the benefit.
